# treemd

A markdown navigator with tree-based structural navigation. Navigate markdown documents using an expandable/collapsible heading tree with a synchronized content view.

![treemd screenshot showing dual-pane interface](assets/output.gif)

## Overview

treemd is a modern markdown viewer that combines the structural clarity of a tree-style outline with powerful interactive navigation. Use it to:

- Navigate large documents by collapsing/expanding heading sections
- Search headings or full document content with highlighted matches
- Edit tables, toggle checkboxes, and follow links without leaving the terminal
- Extract specific sections or query markdown elements with a jq-like syntax
- Pipe markdown from stdin for shell-scripted workflows

## Features

- Dual-pane interface: outline + synchronized content view
- Interactive mode: navigate, edit, and interact with tables, checkboxes, links, and code blocks
- Table editing and navigation
- Checkbox toggling with optional file updates
- Link following (anchors, files, URLs)
- Search and filter headings or content
- Multiple color themes and customizable keybindings
- CLI mode for scripting and extraction

## Installation

Install using common package managers if available for your platform.

Homebrew (macOS / Linux):

```bash
brew install treemd
```

Arch Linux (pacman):

```bash
pacman -S treemd
```

On systems that provide pre-built packages, prefer the packaged binaries for your platform.

## Usage

### TUI Mode (Interactive)

Launch the interactive interface by running treemd with a file or directory:

```bash
treemd README.md        # Open specific file
treemd .                # Open file picker in current directory
treemd docs/            # Open file picker in specified directory
treemd *.md             # Open file picker with matched files
```

Common navigation keys (typical): j/k, g/G, Enter/Space to expand/collapse, Tab to switch focus, q to quit.

### CLI Mode (Non-Interactive)

List headings:

```bash
treemd -l README.md
```

Show heading tree:

```bash
treemd --tree README.md
```

Extract a section:

```bash
treemd -s "Installation" README.md
```

Filter and level options:

```bash
treemd -l --filter "usage" README.md    # Filter by text
treemd -l -L 2 README.md                # Only ## headings
```

Count and JSON output:

```bash
treemd --count README.md                # Count by level
treemd -l -o json README.md             # JSON output
```

## Query Language

treemd includes a jq-like query language for extracting markdown elements. Use -q to execute queries.

Examples:

```bash
treemd -q '.h' doc.md         # All headings
treemd -q '.h2' doc.md        # Level 2 headings
treemd -q '.code' doc.md      # Code blocks
treemd -q '.link' doc.md      # Links
```

Pipes and functions:

```bash
treemd -q '.h2 | text' doc.md
treemd -q '[.h] | count' doc.md
```

## Configuration

User configuration is stored in a platform-appropriate config file (e.g. under ~/.config/treemd/ on Unix-like systems). Themes and keybindings are customizable via that config.

          Example: -q '.h2' --query-output json

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
</output>

<output>
treemd Query Language (tql)

A jq-like query language for navigating and extracting markdown structure.

ELEMENT SELECTORS
    .h, .heading    All headings (any level)
    .h1 - .h6       Headings by level
    .code           All code blocks
    .code[rust]     Code blocks by language
    .link, .a       All links
    .link[external] External links only
    .img            All images
    .table          All tables
    .list           All lists
    .blockquote     All blockquotes

FILTERS & INDEXING
    .h2[Features]       Heading containing "Features" (fuzzy)
    .h2["Installation"] Heading with exact text
    .h2[0]              First h2
    .h2[-1]             Last h2
    .h2[1:3]            h2s at index 1 and 2
    .h2[:3]             First 3 h2s

HIERARCHY
    .h1 > .h2           Direct child h2s under h1s
    .h1 >> .code        Code blocks anywhere under h1s

PIPES
    .h2 | text          Get heading text (strips ##)
    [.h2] | count       Count all h2s
    .code | lang        Get code block languages
    .link | url         Get link URLs

COLLECTION FUNCTIONS
    count, length       Count elements (alias: len, size)
    first, last         First/last element (alias: head)
    limit(n), take(n)   First n elements
    skip(n), drop(n)    Skip first n elements
    nth(n)              Get element at index
    reverse             Reverse order
    sort                Sort alphabetically
    sort_by(key)        Sort by property
    unique              Remove duplicates
    flatten             Flatten nested arrays
    group_by(key)       Group elements by key
    min, max            Min/max numeric value
    add                 Sum numbers or concat strings

STRING FUNCTIONS
    text                Get text representation
    upper, lower        Case conversion
    trim                Strip whitespace
    split(sep)          Split by separator
    join(sep)           Join with separator
    replace(a, b)       Replace substring
    slugify             URL-friendly slug
    lines, words, chars Count lines/words/chars

FILTER FUNCTIONS
    select(cond)        Keep if condition true (alias: where, filter)
    contains(s)         Contains substring (alias: includes)
    startswith(s)       Starts with prefix
    endswith(s)         Ends with suffix
    matches(regex)      Matches regex pattern
    any, all            Check if any/all truthy
    not                 Negate boolean

CONTENT FUNCTIONS
    content             Section content (for headings)
    md                  Raw markdown
    url, href, src      Get URL/link/image source
    lang                Code block language

AGGREGATION FUNCTIONS
    stats               Document statistics
    levels              Heading count by level
    langs               Code block count by language
    types               Link types count

EXAMPLES
    # List all h2 headings
    treemd -q '.h2' doc.md

    # Get heading text only
    treemd -q '.h2 | text' doc.md

    # Count headings
    treemd -q '[.h2] | count' doc.md

    # First 5 headings
    treemd -q '[.h] | limit(5)' doc.md

    # Filter headings (three equivalent ways)
    treemd -q '.h | select(contains("API"))' doc.md
    treemd -q '.h | where(contains("API"))' doc.md
    treemd -q '.h[API]' doc.md

    # All Rust code blocks
    treemd -q '.code[rust]' doc.md

    # External link URLs
    treemd -q '.link[external] | url' doc.md

    # h2s under "Features" section
    treemd -q '.h1[Features] > .h2' doc.md

    # Group headings by level
    treemd -q '[.h] | group_by("level")' doc.md

    # Document statistics
    treemd -q '. | stats' doc.md

    # JSON output
    treemd -q '.h2' --query-output json doc.md

OUTPUT FORMATS (--query-output)
    plain       Human-readable text (default)
    json        Compact JSON
    json-pretty Pretty-printed JSON (alias: jsonp)
    jsonl       Line-delimited JSON (one per line)
    md          Raw markdown
    tree        Tree structure

For more details, see: https://github.com/epistates/treemd
</output>

## Installation

Install using common package managers if available for your platform.

Homebrew (macOS / Linux):

```bash
brew install treemd
```

Arch Linux (pacman):

```bash
pacman -S treemd
```

On systems that provide pre-built packages, prefer the packaged binaries for your platform.
---
## Usage

### TUI Mode (Interactive)

Launch the interactive interface by running treemd with a file or directory:

```bash
treemd README.md        # Open specific file
treemd .                # Open file picker in current directory
treemd docs/            # Open file picker in specified directory
treemd *.md             # Open file picker with matched files
```

Common navigation keys (typical): j/k, g/G, Enter/Space to expand/collapse, Tab to switch focus, q to quit.

### CLI Mode (Non-Interactive)

List headings:

```bash
treemd -l README.md
```

Show heading tree:

```bash
treemd --tree README.md
```

Extract a section:

```bash
treemd -s "Installation" README.md
```

Filter and level options:

```bash
treemd -l --filter "usage" README.md    # Filter by text
treemd -l -L 2 README.md                # Only ## headings
```

Count and JSON output:

```bash
treemd --count README.md                # Count by level
treemd -l -o json README.md             # JSON output
```
</output>

"""Markdown parsing for treemd clone."""
import re


HEADING_RE = re.compile(r'^(#{1,6})(?:\s+(.*?))?(?:\s+#+)?\s*$')
FENCE_RE = re.compile(r'^(```+|~~~+)')


def strip_markdown(text):
    """Strip markdown formatting from inline text for heading titles."""
    # Remove inline code with backticks (the whole `...` is removed)
    text = re.sub(r'`[^`]*`', '', text)
    # Remove bold/italic markers (** __ * _) but keep inner text
    text = re.sub(r'\*\*(.*?)\*\*', r'\1', text)
    text = re.sub(r'__(.*?)__', r'\1', text)
    text = re.sub(r'\*(.*?)\*', r'\1', text)
    text = re.sub(r'_(.*?)_', r'\1', text)
    # Image ![alt](src) -> alt
    text = re.sub(r'!\[([^\]]*)\]\([^\)]*\)', r'\1', text)
    # Link [text](url) -> text
    text = re.sub(r'\[([^\]]*)\]\([^\)]*\)', r'\1', text)
    return text


def slugify(text):
    """Turn heading text into a URL-friendly slug."""

"""Tree building and rendering."""


def build_tree(headings):
    """Convert a flat list of headings to a nested tree.

    Each node is dict with keys: level, title, title_raw, line, children.
    """
    roots = []
    stack = []  # stack of (level, node)
    for h in headings:
        node = dict(h)
        node['children'] = []
        # Pop stack until we find a parent with lower level
        while stack and stack[-1]['level'] >= node['level']:
            stack.pop()
        if stack:
            stack[-1]['children'].append(node)
        else:
            roots.append(node)
        stack.append(node)
    return roots


def render_tree(roots, prefix='', is_last_chain=None):
    """Render tree with box drawing characters, matching treemd layout.

    Lines look like:
        └──# Title
           ├──## Sub
           │  └──### Deep
    """
    if is_last_chain is None:
        is_last_chain = []
    out = []
    n = len(roots)
    for i, node in enumerate(roots):
        is_last = (i == n - 1)
        # Build prefix from is_last_chain
        pfx_parts = []
        for parent_last in is_last_chain:
            pfx_parts.append('   ' if parent_last else '│  ')
        pfx = ''.join(pfx_parts)
        branch = '└──' if is_last else '├──'
        hashes = '#' * node['level']
        title = node['title']
        # treemd renders heading text with a trailing space always (observable when title is empty)
        # but with a space between hashes and title when not empty. When title empty, still a space.
        line = f"{pfx}{branch}{hashes} {title}"
        out.append(line)
        if node['children']:
            out.extend(render_tree(
                node['children'],
                is_last_chain=is_last_chain + [is_last],
            ))
    return out

def read_input(a):
    """Return (content, source) tuple. source may be a filename or None."""
    if a.files:
        f = a.files[0]
        if f == '-':
            data = sys.stdin.read()
            if not data:
                sys.stderr.write("Error reading input: Empty input provided\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            return data, None
        try:
            with open(f, 'rb') as fp:
                data = fp.read()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            sys.stderr.write("Error reading input: I/O error: No such file or directory (os error 2)\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        except IsADirectoryError:
            # Directory - acts as file picker.
            return FILE_PICKER_CONTENT, None
        except PermissionError:
            sys.stderr.write("Error reading input: I/O error: Permission denied (os error 13)\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        # Check if path is a directory at all.
        if os.path.isdir(f):
            return FILE_PICKER_CONTENT, None
        try:
            return data.decode('utf-8'), f
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            return data.decode('utf-8', errors='replace'), f
    # No file specified: use file picker content (regardless of stdin).
    return FILE_PICKER_CONTENT, None

    headings = mdp.parse_headings(new_text)

        hs = [h for h in hs if h['level'] == a.level]

        hs = [h for h in hs if needle in h['title'].lower()]

    roots = mdtree.build_tree(headings)

def do_query(a, text):
    text, headings = ensure_headings(text)
    expr = a.query.strip()
    fmt = a.query_output or 'plain'
    if fmt == 'jsonp':
        fmt = 'json-pretty'
    if fmt not in ('plain', 'json', 'json-pretty', 'jsonl', 'md', 'tree'):
        sys.stderr.write(f"Error: Unknown output format: {fmt}\n")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Handle [.hN] | count
    m = re.match(r'^\[\.(h|heading|h[1-6])\]\s*\|\s*(count|length|len|size)\s*$', expr)
    if m:
        sel = m.group(1)
        if sel in ('h', 'heading'):
            n = len(headings)
        else:
            lvl = int(sel[1:])
            n = sum(1 for h in headings if h['level'] == lvl)
        print(n)
        return 0

    # Handle `.h | text` or `.hN | text`
    m = re.match(r'^\.(h|heading|h[1-6])\s*\|\s*text\s*$', expr)
    if m:
        sel = m.group(1)
        if sel in ('h', 'heading'):
            result = [h['title'] for h in headings]
        else:
            lvl = int(sel[1:])
            result = [h['title'] for h in headings if h['level'] == lvl]
        _emit_query_result(result, fmt, kind='text')
        return 0

    # Handle `.h` or `.hN`
    m = re.match(r'^\.(h|heading|h[1-6])\s*$', expr)
    if m:
        sel = m.group(1)
        if sel in ('h', 'heading'):
            hs = list(headings)
        else:
            lvl = int(sel[1:])
            hs = [h for h in headings if h['level'] == lvl]
        _emit_query_result(hs, fmt, kind='heading')
        return 0

    # Handle `.link` or `.a` or `.link | url`
    m = re.match(r'^\.(link|a)(?:\s*\|\s*(url|href))?\s*$', expr)
    if m:
        links = _extract_links(text)
        if m.group(2):
            _emit_query_result([l['href'] for l in links], fmt, kind='text')
        else:
            _emit_query_result(links, fmt, kind='link')
        return 0

    # Handle `.code` or `.code | lang`
    m = re.match(r'^\.code(?:\s*\|\s*lang)?\s*$', expr)
    if m:
        codes = _extract_code_blocks(text)
        if '| lang' in expr or expr.endswith('lang'):
            _emit_query_result([c['language'] for c in codes], fmt, kind='text')
        else:
            _emit_query_result(codes, fmt, kind='code')
        return 0

    # Unknown query: empty output
    return 0


def _extract_links(text):
    links = []
    # Inline links: [text](url)
    for m in re.finditer(r'(?<!!)\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)]*)\)', text):
        links.append({
            'text': m.group(1),
            'href': m.group(2),
        })
    return links


def _extract_code_blocks(text):
    codes = []
    lines = text.split('\n')
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        m = re.match(r'^(```+|~~~+)\s*(\S*)', lines[i])
        if m:
            fence = m.group(1)[:3]
            lang = m.group(2) or ''
            body = []
            i += 1
            while i < len(lines) and not lines[i].strip().startswith(fence):
                body.append(lines[i])
                i += 1
            codes.append({
                'language': lang,
                'content': '\n'.join(body),
            })
            i += 1
            continue
        i += 1
    return codes


def _emit_query_result(result, fmt, kind='heading'):
    if fmt == 'plain':
        if kind == 'heading':
            for h in result:
                print(f"{'#' * h['level']} {h['title']}")
        elif kind == 'link':
            for l in result:
                print(f"[{l['text']}]({l['href']})")
        elif kind == 'code':
            for c in result:
                print(f"```{c['language']}")
                print(c['content'])
                print("```")
        else:  # text
            for s in result:
                print(s)
        return
    # JSON variants
    def to_obj(item):
        if kind == 'heading':
            return {
                'type': 'heading',
                'level': item['level'],
                'text': item['title'],
                'line': item['line'],
            }
        if kind == 'link':
            return {'type': 'link', 'text': item['text'], 'href': item['href']}
        if kind == 'code':
            return {'type': 'code', 'language': item['language'], 'content': item['content']}
        return item
    arr = [to_obj(x) for x in result]
    if fmt == 'json':
        print(json.dumps(arr, separators=(',', ':')))
    elif fmt == 'json-pretty':
        print(json.dumps(arr, indent=2))
    elif fmt == 'jsonl':
        for x in arr:
            print(json.dumps(x, separators=(',', ':')))
    elif fmt == 'md':
        # raw markdown reconstruction
        for x in result:
            if kind == 'heading':
                print(f"{'#' * x['level']} {x['title']}")
            elif kind == 'link':
                print(f"[{x['text']}]({x['href']})")
            elif kind == 'code':
                print(f"```{x['language']}\n{x['content']}\n```")
            else:
                print(x)
    elif fmt == 'tree':
        for x in result:
            if kind == 'heading':
                print(f"{'  ' * (x['level'] - 1)}{'#' * x['level']} {x['title']}")
            else:
                print(x)

def do_setup_completions():
    shell_env = os.environ.get('SHELL', '')
    shell_name = os.path.basename(shell_env)
    completions_help = """Shell Completion Setup Instructions

Add the appropriate line to your shell config:

Fish (~/.config/fish/config.fish):

After adding the line, restart your shell or source the config file.
"""
    if shell_name not in ('bash', 'zsh', 'fish'):
        sys.stderr.write("Error setting up completions: Could not detect shell\n")
        print(completions_help, end='')
        sys.exit(1)
    home = os.path.expanduser('~')
    if shell_name == 'bash':
        cfg = os.path.join(home, '.bashrc')

    elif shell_name == 'zsh':
        cfg = os.path.join(home, '.zshrc')
        line = '  source <(COMPLETE=zsh treemd)'

        line = '  COMPLETE=fish treemd | source'
    print(f"Detected shell: {shell_name}")
    print()
    print(f'To enable shell completions, add this line to "{cfg}":')
    print(line)

    try:
        ans = input("Would you like to add it automatically? (y/N): ").strip().lower()
    except EOFError:
        ans = ''
    print()
    if ans == 'y' or ans == 'yes':
        try:
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(cfg), exist_ok=True)

            if os.path.isfile(cfg):
                with open(cfg, 'r') as fp:
                    existing = fp.read()
            if line.strip() in existing:
                print("Completions already configured.")
            else:

    levels              Heading count by level
    langs               Code block count by language
    types               Link types count

EXAMPLES
    # List all h2 headings
    treemd -q '.h2' doc.md

    # Get heading text only
    treemd -q '.h2 | text' doc.md

    # Count headings
    treemd -q '[.h2] | count' doc.md

    # First 5 headings
    treemd -q '[.h] | limit(5)' doc.md

    # Filter headings (three equivalent ways)
    treemd -q '.h | select(contains("API"))' doc.md
    treemd -q '.h | where(contains("API"))' doc.md
    treemd -q '.h[API]' doc.md

    # All Rust code blocks
    treemd -q '.code[rust]' doc.md

    # External link URLs
    treemd -q '.link[external] | url' doc.md

    # h2s under "Features" section
    treemd -q '.h1[Features] > .h2' doc.md

    # Group headings by level
    treemd -q '[.h] | group_by("level")' doc.md

    # Document statistics
    treemd -q '. | stats' doc.md

    # JSON output
    treemd -q '.h2' --query-output json doc.md

OUTPUT FORMATS (--query-output)
    plain       Human-readable text (default)
    json        Compact JSON
    json-pretty Pretty-printed JSON (alias: jsonp)
    jsonl       Line-delimited JSON (one per line)
    md          Raw markdown
    tree        Tree structure

For more details, see: https://github.com/epistates/treemd
"""

def die_clap(msg, code=2):
    sys.stderr.write(f"error: {msg}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
    sys.exit(code)


class Args:
    def __init__(self):
        self.files = []
        self.list = False
        self.tree = False
        self.filter = None
        self.level = None
        self.output = None
        self.section = None
        self.count = False
        self.setup_completions = False
        self.theme = None
        self.color_mode = None
        self.no_images = False
        self.images = False
        self.query = None
        self.query_help = False
        self.query_output = None
        self.subcommand = None  # 'at-line' or 'help'
        self.subargs = []
        self.help_short = False
        self.help_long = False
        self.version = False


OPTIONS_WITH_VALUES = {
    '--filter', '--level', '-L',
    '--output', '-o', '--section', '-s',
    '--theme', '--color-mode',
    '--query', '-q', '--query-output',
}

POSSIBLE_OUTPUT = {'plain', 'json', 'tree'}
POSSIBLE_COLOR = {'auto', 'rgb', '256'}


def parse_args(argv):
    a = Args()
    i = 0
    # Subcommands end positional parsing.
    # First, look for 'at-line' or 'help' subcommand at any position before a file path? Actually clap puts subcommand after options.
    # Let's mimic clap: process flags; if token matches subcommand name, enter subcommand parsing.
    while i < len(argv):
        tok = argv[i]
        if tok == '--':
            i += 1
            while i < len(argv):
                a.files.append(argv[i])
                i += 1
            break
        if tok == '-h':
            a.help_short = True
            i += 1
        elif tok == '--help':
            a.help_long = True
            i += 1
        elif tok in ('-V', '--version'):
            a.version = True
            i += 1
        elif tok in ('-l', '--list'):
            a.list = True
            i += 1
        elif tok == '--tree':
            a.tree = True
            i += 1
        elif tok == '--count':
            a.count = True
            i += 1
        elif tok == '--setup-completions':
            a.setup_completions = True
            i += 1
        elif tok == '--no-images':
            a.no_images = True
            i += 1
        elif tok == '--images':
            a.images = True
            i += 1
        elif tok == '--query-help':
            a.query_help = True
            i += 1
        elif tok.startswith('--filter='):
            a.filter = tok[len('--filter='):]
            i += 1
        elif tok == '--filter':
            if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                die_clap("a value is required for '--filter <PATTERN>' but none was supplied")
            a.filter = argv[i + 1]
            i += 2
        elif tok in ('-L', '--level') or tok.startswith('--level='):
            if tok.startswith('--level='):
                val = tok[len('--level='):]
                i += 1
            else:
                if i + 1 >= len(argv) or argv[i + 1].startswith('-'):
                    die_clap(f"a value is required for '--level <LEVEL>' but none was supplied")
                val = argv[i + 1]
                i += 2
            try:
                a.level = int(val)
            except ValueError:
                die_clap(f"invalid value '{val}' for '--level <LEVEL>': invalid digit found in string")
        elif tok in ('-o', '--output') or tok.startswith('--output='):
            if tok.startswith('--output='):
                val = tok[len('--output='):]
                i += 1
            else:
                if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                    die_clap(f"a value is required for '--output <OUTPUT>' but none was supplied")
                val = argv[i + 1]
                i += 2
            if val not in POSSIBLE_OUTPUT:
                die_clap(f"invalid value '{val}' for '--output <OUTPUT>'\n  [possible values: plain, json, tree]")
            a.output = val
        elif tok in ('-s', '--section') or tok.startswith('--section='):
            if tok.startswith('--section='):
                val = tok[len('--section='):]
                i += 1
            else:
                if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                    die_clap(f"a value is required for '--section <HEADING>' but none was supplied")
                val = argv[i + 1]
                i += 2
            a.section = val
        elif tok == '--theme' or tok.startswith('--theme='):
            if tok.startswith('--theme='):
                a.theme = tok[len('--theme='):]
                i += 1
            else:
                if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                    die_clap(f"a value is required for '--theme <THEME>' but none was supplied")
                a.theme = argv[i + 1]
                i += 2
        elif tok == '--color-mode' or tok.startswith('--color-mode='):
            if tok.startswith('--color-mode='):
                val = tok[len('--color-mode='):]
                i += 1
            else:
                if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                    die_clap(f"a value is required for '--color-mode <MODE>' but none was supplied")
                val = argv[i + 1]
                i += 2
            if val not in POSSIBLE_COLOR:
                die_clap(f"invalid value '{val}' for '--color-mode <MODE>'\n  [possible values: auto, rgb, 256]")
            a.color_mode = val
        elif tok in ('-q', '--query') or tok.startswith('--query='):
            if tok.startswith('--query='):
                a.query = tok[len('--query='):]
                i += 1
            else:
                if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                    die_clap(f"a value is required for '--query <EXPR>' but none was supplied")
                a.query = argv[i + 1]
                i += 2
        elif tok == '--query-output' or tok.startswith('--query-output='):
            if tok.startswith('--query-output='):
                a.query_output = tok[len('--query-output='):]
                i += 1
            else:
                if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                    die_clap(f"a value is required for '--query-output <FORMAT>' but none was supplied")
                a.query_output = argv[i + 1]
                i += 2
        elif tok == 'at-line':
            a.subcommand = 'at-line'
            i += 1
            a.subargs = argv[i:]
            break
        elif tok == 'help':
            a.subcommand = 'help'
            i += 1
            a.subargs = argv[i:]
            break
        elif tok.startswith('-') and tok != '-':
            die_clap(f"unexpected argument '{tok}' found")
        else:
            a.files.append(tok)
            i += 1
    return a


def read_input(a):
    """Return (content, source) tuple. source may be a filename or None."""
    if a.files:
        f = a.files[0]
        if f == '-':
            data = sys.stdin.read()
            if not data:
                sys.stderr.write("Error reading input: Empty input provided\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            return data, None
        try:
            with open(f, 'rb') as fp:
                data = fp.read()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            sys.stderr.write("Error reading input: I/O error: No such file or directory (os error 2)\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        except IsADirectoryError:
            # Directory - acts as file picker.
            return FILE_PICKER_CONTENT, None
        except PermissionError:
            sys.stderr.write("Error reading input: I/O error: Permission denied (os error 13)\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        # Check if path is a directory at all.
        if os.path.isdir(f):
            return FILE_PICKER_CONTENT, None
        try:
            return data.decode('utf-8'), f
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            return data.decode('utf-8', errors='replace'), f
    # No file specified: use file picker content (regardless of stdin).
    return FILE_PICKER_CONTENT, None


def ensure_headings(text):
    """Parse headings; if none, inject '# Input' as virtual heading."""
    headings = mdp.parse_headings(text)
    if headings:
        return text, headings
    # Fallback: add a virtual "# Input" heading at the start
    new_text = "# Input\n" + text if text else "# Input\n"
    headings = mdp.parse_headings(new_text)
    return new_text, headings


def do_list(a, text):
    text, headings = ensure_headings(text)
    out_fmt = a.output or 'plain'
    if out_fmt == 'tree':
        sys.stderr.write("Use --tree for tree output\n")
        sys.exit(1)
    if out_fmt == 'json':
        roots = mdtree.build_tree(headings)
        print(mdout.list_json(text, headings, roots))
        return 0
    # plain
    hs = headings
    if a.level is not None:
        hs = [h for h in hs if h['level'] == a.level]
    elif a.filter:
        needle = a.filter.lower()
        hs = [h for h in hs if needle in h['title'].lower()]
    if hs:
        print('\n'.join(mdout.format_heading_line(h) for h in hs))
    return 0


def do_tree(a, text):
    text, headings = ensure_headings(text)
    out_fmt = a.output or 'plain'
    if out_fmt == 'json':
        print(mdout.tree_json(headings))
        return 0
    # plain or tree: always same output
    roots = mdtree.build_tree(headings)
    print(mdout.tree_plain(roots))
    return 0

def do_query(a, text):
    text, headings = ensure_headings(text)
    expr = a.query.strip()
    fmt = a.query_output or 'plain'
    if fmt == 'jsonp':
        fmt = 'json-pretty'
    if fmt not in ('plain', 'json', 'json-pretty', 'jsonl', 'md', 'tree'):
        sys.stderr.write(f"Error: Unknown output format: {fmt}\n")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Handle [.hN] | count
    m = re.match(r'^\[\.(h|heading|h[1-6])\]\s*\|\s*(count|length|len|size)\s*$', expr)
    if m:
        sel = m.group(1)
        if sel in ('h', 'heading'):
            n = len(headings)
        else:
            lvl = int(sel[1:])
            n = sum(1 for h in headings if h['level'] == lvl)
        print(n)
        return 0

    # Handle `.h | text` or `.hN | text`
    m = re.match(r'^\.(h|heading|h[1-6])\s*\|\s*text\s*$', expr)
    if m:
        sel = m.group(1)
        if sel in ('h', 'heading'):
            result = [h['title'] for h in headings]
        else:
            lvl = int(sel[1:])
            result = [h['title'] for h in headings if h['level'] == lvl]
        _emit_query_result(result, fmt, kind='text')
        return 0

    # Handle `.h` or `.hN`
    m = re.match(r'^\.(h|heading|h[1-6])\s*$', expr)
    if m:
        sel = m.group(1)
        if sel in ('h', 'heading'):
            hs = list(headings)
        else:
            lvl = int(sel[1:])
            hs = [h for h in headings if h['level'] == lvl]
        _emit_query_result(hs, fmt, kind='heading')
        return 0

    # Handle `.link` or `.a` or `.link | url`
    m = re.match(r'^\.(link|a)(?:\s*\|\s*(url|href))?\s*$', expr)
    if m:
        links = _extract_links(text)
        if m.group(2):
            _emit_query_result([l['href'] for l in links], fmt, kind='text')
        else:
            _emit_query_result(links, fmt, kind='link')
        return 0

    # Handle `.code` or `.code | lang`
    m = re.match(r'^\.code(?:\s*\|\s*lang)?\s*$', expr)
    if m:
        codes = _extract_code_blocks(text)
        if '| lang' in expr or expr.endswith('lang'):
            _emit_query_result([c['language'] for c in codes], fmt, kind='text')
        else:
            _emit_query_result(codes, fmt, kind='code')
        return 0

    # Unknown query: empty output
    return 0


def _extract_links(text):
    links = []
    # Inline links: [text](url)
    for m in re.finditer(r'(?<!!)\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)]*)\)', text):
        links.append({
            'text': m.group(1),
            'href': m.group(2),
        })
    return links


def _extract_code_blocks(text):
    codes = []
    lines = text.split('\n')
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        m = re.match(r'^(```+|~~~+)\s*(\S*)', lines[i])
        if m:
            fence = m.group(1)[:3]
            lang = m.group(2) or ''
            body = []
            i += 1
            while i < len(lines) and not lines[i].strip().startswith(fence):
                body.append(lines[i])
                i += 1
            codes.append({
                'language': lang,
                'content': '\n'.join(body),
            })
            i += 1
            continue
        i += 1
    return codes


def _emit_query_result(result, fmt, kind='heading'):
    if fmt == 'plain':
        if kind == 'heading':
            for h in result:
                print(f"{'#' * h['level']} {h['title']}")
        elif kind == 'link':
            for l in result:
                print(f"[{l['text']}]({l['href']})")
        elif kind == 'code':
            for c in result:
                print(f"```{c['language']}")
                print(c['content'])
                print("```")
        else:  # text
            for s in result:
                print(s)
        return
    # JSON variants
    def to_obj(item):
        if kind == 'heading':
            return {
                'type': 'heading',
                'level': item['level'],
                'text': item['title'],
                'line': item['line'],
            }
        if kind == 'link':
            return {'type': 'link', 'text': item['text'], 'href': item['href']}
        if kind == 'code':
            return {'type': 'code', 'language': item['language'], 'content': item['content']}
        return item
    arr = [to_obj(x) for x in result]
    if fmt == 'json':
        print(json.dumps(arr, separators=(',', ':')))
    elif fmt == 'json-pretty':
        print(json.dumps(arr, indent=2))
    elif fmt == 'jsonl':
        for x in arr:
            print(json.dumps(x, separators=(',', ':')))
    elif fmt == 'md':
        # raw markdown reconstruction
        for x in result:
            if kind == 'heading':
                print(f"{'#' * x['level']} {x['title']}")
            elif kind == 'link':
                print(f"[{x['text']}]({x['href']})")
            elif kind == 'code':
                print(f"```{x['language']}\n{x['content']}\n```")
            else:
                print(x)
    elif fmt == 'tree':
        for x in result:
            if kind == 'heading':
                print(f"{'  ' * (x['level'] - 1)}{'#' * x['level']} {x['title']}")
            else:
                print(x)

def do_setup_completions():
    shell_env = os.environ.get('SHELL', '')
    shell_name = os.path.basename(shell_env)
    completions_help = """Shell Completion Setup Instructions

Add the appropriate line to your shell config:

Bash (~/.bashrc):
  source <(COMPLETE=bash treemd)

Zsh (~/.zshrc):
  source <(COMPLETE=zsh treemd)

Fish (~/.config/fish/config.fish):
  COMPLETE=fish treemd | source

After adding the line, restart your shell or source the config file.
"""
    if shell_name not in ('bash', 'zsh', 'fish'):
        sys.stderr.write("Error setting up completions: Could not detect shell\n")
        print(completions_help, end='')
        sys.exit(1)
    home = os.path.expanduser('~')
    if shell_name == 'bash':
        cfg = os.path.join(home, '.bashrc')
        line = '  source <(COMPLETE=bash treemd)'
    elif shell_name == 'zsh':
        cfg = os.path.join(home, '.zshrc')
        line = '  source <(COMPLETE=zsh treemd)'
    else:  # fish
        cfg = os.path.join(home, '.config/fish/config.fish')
        line = '  COMPLETE=fish treemd | source'
    print(f"Detected shell: {shell_name}")
    print()
    print(f'To enable shell completions, add this line to "{cfg}":')
    print(line)
    print()
    try:
        ans = input("Would you like to add it automatically? (y/N): ").strip().lower()
    except EOFError:
        ans = ''
    print()
    if ans == 'y' or ans == 'yes':
        try:
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(cfg), exist_ok=True)
            existing = ''
            if os.path.isfile(cfg):
                with open(cfg, 'r') as fp:
                    existing = fp.read()
            if line.strip() in existing:
                print("Completions already configured.")
            else:
                with open(cfg, 'a') as fp:
                    if existing and not existing.endswith('\n'):
                        fp.write('\n')
                    fp.write('\n# treemd completions\n')
                    fp.write(line.strip() + '\n')
                print(f"Added completions to {cfg}. Restart your shell or source the file.")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Failed to add completion: {e}")
            sys.exit(1)
    else:
        print("Manually add the line above to enable completions.")
    return 0

def main(argv=None):
    if argv is None:
        argv = sys.argv[1:]

    # Handle completion dynamic mode
    comp = os.environ.get('COMPLETE')
    if comp in ('bash', 'zsh', 'fish'):
        return do_completion_script(comp)

    a = parse_args(argv)

    if a.help_short:
        sys.stdout.write(SHORT_HELP)
        return 0
    if a.help_long:
        sys.stdout.write(LONG_HELP)
        return 0
    if a.version:
        print(VERSION)
        return 0
    if a.subcommand == 'help':
        if not a.subargs:
            sys.stdout.write(HELP_CMD_MSG)
            return 0
        sub = a.subargs[0]
        if sub == 'at-line':
            sys.stdout.write(AT_LINE_HELP_LONG)
            return 0
        if sub == 'help':
            sys.stdout.write(HELP_CMD_MSG)
            return 0
        die_clap(f"unrecognized subcommand '{sub}'")
    if a.subcommand == 'at-line':
        # parse subargs
        if not a.subargs:
            sys.stderr.write("error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  <LINE>\n\nUsage: executable at-line <LINE>\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
            return 2
        arg0 = a.subargs[0]
        if arg0 in ('-h',):
            sys.stdout.write(AT_LINE_HELP_SHORT)
            return 0
        if arg0 in ('--help',):
            sys.stdout.write(AT_LINE_HELP_LONG)
            return 0
        # extra args
        extras = [x for x in a.subargs[1:] if not x.startswith('-')]
        if extras:
            die_clap(f"unexpected argument '{extras[0]}' found")
        try:
            line = int(arg0)
        except ValueError:
            die_clap(f"invalid value '{arg0}' for '<LINE>': invalid digit found in string")
        # Read stdin (if piped) and find heading at or before this line.

def read_input(a):
    """Return (content, source) tuple. source may be a filename or None."""
    if a.files:
        f = a.files[0]
        if f == '-':
            data = sys.stdin.read()
            if not data:
                sys.stderr.write("Error reading input: Empty input provided\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            return data, None
        try:
            with open(f, 'rb') as fp:
                data = fp.read()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            sys.stderr.write("Error reading input: I/O error: No such file or directory (os error 2)\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        except IsADirectoryError:
            # Directory - acts as file picker.
            return FILE_PICKER_CONTENT, None
        except PermissionError:
            sys.stderr.write("Error reading input: I/O error: Permission denied (os error 13)\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        # Check if path is a directory at all.
        if os.path.isdir(f):
            return FILE_PICKER_CONTENT, None
        try:
            return data.decode('utf-8'), f
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            return data.decode('utf-8', errors='replace'), f

    m = re.match(r'^\.code(?:\s*\|\s*lang)?\s*$', expr)
    if m:
        codes = _extract_code_blocks(text)
        if '| lang' in expr or expr.endswith('lang'):
            _emit_query_result([c['language'] for c in codes], fmt, kind='text')
        else:
            _emit_query_result(codes, fmt, kind='code')
        return 0

    # Unknown query: empty output
    return 0


def _extract_links(text):
    links = []
    # Inline links: [text](url)
    for m in re.finditer(r'(?<!!)\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)]*)\)', text):
        links.append({
            'text': m.group(1),
            'href': m.group(2),
        })
    return links


def _extract_code_blocks(text):
    codes = []
    lines = text.split('\n')
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        m = re.match(r'^(```+|~~~+)\s*(\S*)', lines[i])
        if m:
            fence = m.group(1)[:3]
            lang = m.group(2) or ''
            body = []
            i += 1
            while i < len(lines) and not lines[i].strip().startswith(fence):
                body.append(lines[i])
                i += 1
            codes.append({
                'language': lang,
                'content': '\n'.join(body),
            })
            i += 1
            continue
        i += 1
    return codes


def _emit_query_result(result, fmt, kind='heading'):
    if fmt == 'plain':
        if kind == 'heading':
            for h in result:
                print(f"{'#' * h['level']} {h['title']}")
        elif kind == 'link':
            for l in result:
                print(f"[{l['text']}]({l['href']})")
        elif kind == 'code':
            for c in result:
                print(f"```{c['language']}")
                print(c['content'])
                print("```")
        else:  # text
            for s in result:
                print(s)
        return
    # JSON variants
    def to_obj(item):
        if kind == 'heading':
            return {
                'type': 'heading',
                'level': item['level'],
                'text': item['title'],
                'line': item['line'],
            }
        if kind == 'link':
            return {'type': 'link', 'text': item['text'], 'href': item['href']}
        if kind == 'code':
            return {'type': 'code', 'language': item['language'], 'content': item['content']}
        return item
    arr = [to_obj(x) for x in result]
    if fmt == 'json':
        print(json.dumps(arr, separators=(',', ':')))
    elif fmt == 'json-pretty':
        print(json.dumps(arr, indent=2))
    elif fmt == 'jsonl':
        for x in arr:
            print(json.dumps(x, separators=(',', ':')))
    elif fmt == 'md':
        # raw markdown reconstruction
        for x in result:
            if kind == 'heading':
                print(f"{'#' * x['level']} {x['title']}")
            elif kind == 'link':
                print(f"[{x['text']}]({x['href']})")
            elif kind == 'code':
                print(f"```{x['language']}\n{x['content']}\n```")
            else:
                print(x)
    elif fmt == 'tree':
        for x in result:
            if kind == 'heading':
                print(f"{'  ' * (x['level'] - 1)}{'#' * x['level']} {x['title']}")
            else:
                print(x)

def do_setup_completions():
    shell_env = os.environ.get('SHELL', '')
    shell_name = os.path.basename(shell_env)
    completions_help = """Shell Completion Setup Instructions

Add the appropriate line to your shell config:

Bash (~/.bashrc):
  source <(COMPLETE=bash treemd)

Zsh (~/.zshrc):
  source <(COMPLETE=zsh treemd)

Fish (~/.config/fish/config.fish):
  COMPLETE=fish treemd | source

After adding the line, restart your shell or source the config file.
"""
    if shell_name not in ('bash', 'zsh', 'fish'):
        sys.stderr.write("Error setting up completions: Could not detect shell\n")
        print(completions_help, end='')
        sys.exit(1)
    home = os.path.expanduser('~')
    if shell_name == 'bash':
        cfg = os.path.join(home, '.bashrc')
        line = '  source <(COMPLETE=bash treemd)'
    elif shell_name == 'zsh':
        cfg = os.path.join(home, '.zshrc')
        line = '  source <(COMPLETE=zsh treemd)'
    else:  # fish
        cfg = os.path.join(home, '.config/fish/config.fish')
        line = '  COMPLETE=fish treemd | source'
    print(f"Detected shell: {shell_name}")
    print()
    print(f'To enable shell completions, add this line to "{cfg}":')
    print(line)
    print()
    try:
        ans = input("Would you like to add it automatically? (y/N): ").strip().lower()
    except EOFError:
        ans = ''
    print()
    if ans == 'y' or ans == 'yes':
        try:
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(cfg), exist_ok=True)
            existing = ''
            if os.path.isfile(cfg):
                with open(cfg, 'r') as fp:
                    existing = fp.read()
            if line.strip() in existing:
                print("Completions already configured.")
            else:
                with open(cfg, 'a') as fp:
                    if existing and not existing.endswith('\n'):
                        fp.write('\n')
                    fp.write('\n# treemd completions\n')
                    fp.write(line.strip() + '\n')
                print(f"Added completions to {cfg}. Restart your shell or source the file.")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Failed to add completion: {e}")
            sys.exit(1)
    else:
        print("Manually add the line above to enable completions.")
    return 0


def do_completion_script(shell):

def main(argv=None):
    if argv is None:
        argv = sys.argv[1:]

    # Handle completion dynamic mode
    comp = os.environ.get('COMPLETE')
    if comp in ('bash', 'zsh', 'fish'):
        return do_completion_script(comp)

    a = parse_args(argv)

    if a.help_short:
        sys.stdout.write(SHORT_HELP)
        return 0
    if a.help_long:
        sys.stdout.write(LONG_HELP)
        return 0
    if a.version:
        print(VERSION)
        return 0
    if a.subcommand == 'help':
        if not a.subargs:
            sys.stdout.write(HELP_CMD_MSG)
            return 0
        sub = a.subargs[0]
        if sub == 'at-line':
            sys.stdout.write(AT_LINE_HELP_LONG)
            return 0
        if sub == 'help':
            sys.stdout.write(HELP_CMD_MSG)
            return 0
        die_clap(f"unrecognized subcommand '{sub}'")
    if a.subcommand == 'at-line':
        # parse subargs
        if not a.subargs:
            sys.stderr.write("error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  <LINE>\n\nUsage: executable at-line <LINE>\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
            return 2
        arg0 = a.subargs[0]
        if arg0 in ('-h',):
            sys.stdout.write(AT_LINE_HELP_SHORT)
            return 0
        if arg0 in ('--help',):
            sys.stdout.write(AT_LINE_HELP_LONG)
            return 0
        # extra args
        extras = [x for x in a.subargs[1:] if not x.startswith('-')]
        if extras:
            die_clap(f"unexpected argument '{extras[0]}' found")
        try:
            line = int(arg0)
        except ValueError:
            die_clap(f"invalid value '{arg0}' for '<LINE>': invalid digit found in string")
        # Read stdin (if piped) and find heading at or before this line.
        # In our context the binary outputs nothing for at-line if no stdin tty; just return empty.
        if not sys.stdin.isatty():
            try:
                text = sys.stdin.read()
            except Exception:
                text = ''
            if text:
                headings = mdp.parse_headings(text)
                selected = None
                for h in headings:
                    if h['line'] <= line:
                        selected = h
                    else:
                        break
                if selected:
                    print(f"{'#' * selected['level']} {selected['title']}")
        return 0

    if a.query_help:
        sys.stdout.write(QUERY_HELP)
        return 0
    if a.setup_completions:
        return do_setup_completions()

    # Determine action precedence.
    if a.query is not None:
        text, _src = read_input(a)
        return do_query(a, text)
    if a.section is not None:
        text, _src = read_input(a)
        return do_section(a, text)
    if a.count:
        text, _src = read_input(a)
        return do_count(a, text)
    if a.tree:
        text, _src = read_input(a)
        return do_tree(a, text)
    if a.list:
        text, _src = read_input(a)
        return do_list(a, text)

    # No CLI flag given: TUI mode (error without tty).
    do_tui_error()
    return 1

def parse_args(argv):
    a = Args()
    i = 0
    # Subcommands end positional parsing.
    # First, look for 'at-line' or 'help' subcommand at any position before a file path? Actually clap puts subcommand after options.
    # Let's mimic clap: process flags; if token matches subcommand name, enter subcommand parsing.
    while i < len(argv):
        tok = argv[i]
        if tok == '--':
            i += 1
            while i < len(argv):
                a.files.append(argv[i])
                i += 1
            break
        if tok == '-h':
            a.help_short = True
            i += 1
        elif tok == '--help':
            a.help_long = True
            i += 1
        elif tok in ('-V', '--version'):
            a.version = True
            i += 1
        elif tok in ('-l', '--list'):
            a.list = True
            i += 1
        elif tok == '--tree':
            a.tree = True
            i += 1
        elif tok == '--count':
            a.count = True
            i += 1
        elif tok == '--setup-completions':
            a.setup_completions = True
            i += 1
        elif tok == '--no-images':
            a.no_images = True
            i += 1
        elif tok == '--images':
            a.images = True
            i += 1
        elif tok == '--query-help':
            a.query_help = True
            i += 1
        elif tok.startswith('--filter='):
            a.filter = tok[len('--filter='):]
            i += 1
        elif tok == '--filter':
            if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                die_clap("a value is required for '--filter <PATTERN>' but none was supplied")
            a.filter = argv[i + 1]
            i += 2
        elif tok in ('-L', '--level') or tok.startswith('--level='):
            if tok.startswith('--level='):
                val = tok[len('--level='):]
                i += 1
            else:
                if i + 1 >= len(argv) or argv[i + 1].startswith('-'):
                    die_clap(f"a value is required for '--level <LEVEL>' but none was supplied")
                val = argv[i + 1]
                i += 2
            try:
                a.level = int(val)
            except ValueError:
                die_clap(f"invalid value '{val}' for '--level <LEVEL>': invalid digit found in string")
        elif tok in ('-o', '--output') or tok.startswith('--output='):
            if tok.startswith('--output='):
                val = tok[len('--output='):]
                i += 1
            else:
                if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                    die_clap(f"a value is required for '--output <OUTPUT>' but none was supplied")
                val = argv[i + 1]
                i += 2
            if val not in POSSIBLE_OUTPUT:
                die_clap(f"invalid value '{val}' for '--output <OUTPUT>'\n  [possible values: plain, json, tree]")
            a.output = val
        elif tok in ('-s', '--section') or tok.startswith('--section='):
            if tok.startswith('--section='):
                val = tok[len('--section='):]
                i += 1
            else:
                if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                    die_clap(f"a value is required for '--section <HEADING>' but none was supplied")
                val = argv[i + 1]
                i += 2
            a.section = val
        elif tok == '--theme' or tok.startswith('--theme='):
            if tok.startswith('--theme='):
                a.theme = tok[len('--theme='):]
                i += 1
            else:
                if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                    die_clap(f"a value is required for '--theme <THEME>' but none was supplied")
                a.theme = argv[i + 1]
                i += 2
        elif tok == '--color-mode' or tok.startswith('--color-mode='):
            if tok.startswith('--color-mode='):
                val = tok[len('--color-mode='):]
                i += 1
            else:
                if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                    die_clap(f"a value is required for '--color-mode <MODE>' but none was supplied")
                val = argv[i + 1]
                i += 2
            if val not in POSSIBLE_COLOR:
                die_clap(f"invalid value '{val}' for '--color-mode <MODE>'\n  [possible values: auto, rgb, 256]")
            a.color_mode = val
        elif tok in ('-q', '--query') or tok.startswith('--query='):
            if tok.startswith('--query='):
                a.query = tok[len('--query='):]
                i += 1
            else:
                if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                    die_clap(f"a value is required for '--query <EXPR>' but none was supplied")
                a.query = argv[i + 1]
                i += 2
        elif tok == '--query-output' or tok.startswith('--query-output='):
            if tok.startswith('--query-output='):
                a.query_output = tok[len('--query-output='):]
                i += 1
            else:
                if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                    die_clap(f"a value is required for '--query-output <FORMAT>' but none was supplied")
                a.query_output = argv[i + 1]
                i += 2
        elif tok == 'at-line':
            a.subcommand = 'at-line'
            i += 1
            a.subargs = argv[i:]
            break
        elif tok == 'help':
            a.subcommand = 'help'
            i += 1
            a.subargs = argv[i:]
            break
        elif tok.startswith('-') and tok != '-':
            die_clap(f"unexpected argument '{tok}' found")
        else:
            a.files.append(tok)
            i += 1
    return a


def read_input(a):
    """Return (content, source) tuple. source may be a filename or None."""
    if a.files:
        f = a.files[0]
        if f == '-':
            data = sys.stdin.read()
            if not data:
                sys.stderr.write("Error reading input: Empty input provided\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            return data, None
        try:
            with open(f, 'rb') as fp:
                data = fp.read()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            sys.stderr.write("Error reading input: I/O error: No such file or directory (os error 2)\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        except IsADirectoryError:
            # Directory - acts as file picker.
            return FILE_PICKER_CONTENT, None
        except PermissionError:
            sys.stderr.write("Error reading input: I/O error: Permission denied (os error 13)\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        # Check if path is a directory at all.
        if os.path.isdir(f):
            return FILE_PICKER_CONTENT, None
        try:
            return data.decode('utf-8'), f
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            return data.decode('utf-8', errors='replace'), f
    # No file specified: use file picker content (regardless of stdin).
    return FILE_PICKER_CONTENT, None


def ensure_headings(text):
    """Parse headings; if none, inject '# Input' as virtual heading."""
    headings = mdp.parse_headings(text)
    if headings:
        return text, headings
    # Fallback: add a virtual "# Input" heading at the start
    new_text = "# Input\n" + text if text else "# Input\n"
    headings = mdp.parse_headings(new_text)
    return new_text, headings


def do_list(a, text):
    text, headings = ensure_headings(text)
    out_fmt = a.output or 'plain'
    if out_fmt == 'tree':
        sys.stderr.write("Use --tree for tree output\n")
        sys.exit(1)
    if out_fmt == 'json':
        roots = mdtree.build_tree(headings)
        print(mdout.list_json(text, headings, roots))
        return 0
    # plain
    hs = headings
    if a.level is not None:
        hs = [h for h in hs if h['level'] == a.level]
    elif a.filter:

        hs = [h for h in hs if needle in h['title'].lower()]
    if hs:
        print('\n'.join(mdout.format_heading_line(h) for h in hs))

def do_tree(a, text):

    roots = mdtree.build_tree(headings)

def do_section(a, text):
    text, headings = ensure_headings(text)

    if result is None:
        print(f"Section '{a.section}' not found")

def do_query(a, text):
    text, headings = ensure_headings(text)
    expr = a.query.strip()
    fmt = a.query_output or 'plain'
    if fmt == 'jsonp':
        fmt = 'json-pretty'
    if fmt not in ('plain', 'json', 'json-pretty', 'jsonl', 'md', 'tree'):
        sys.stderr.write(f"Error: Unknown output format: {fmt}\n")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Handle [.hN] | count
    m = re.match(r'^\[\.(h|heading|h[1-6])\]\s*\|\s*(count|length|len|size)\s*$', expr)
    if m:
        sel = m.group(1)
        if sel in ('h', 'heading'):
            n = len(headings)
        else:
            lvl = int(sel[1:])
            n = sum(1 for h in headings if h['level'] == lvl)
        print(n)
        return 0

    # Handle `.h | text` or `.hN | text`
    m = re.match(r'^\.(h|heading|h[1-6])\s*\|\s*text\s*$', expr)
    if m:
        sel = m.group(1)
        if sel in ('h', 'heading'):
            result = [h['title'] for h in headings]
        else:
            lvl = int(sel[1:])
            result = [h['title'] for h in headings if h['level'] == lvl]
        _emit_query_result(result, fmt, kind='text')
        return 0

    # Handle `.h` or `.hN`
    m = re.match(r'^\.(h|heading|h[1-6])\s*$', expr)
    if m:
        sel = m.group(1)
        if sel in ('h', 'heading'):
            hs = list(headings)
        else:
            lvl = int(sel[1:])
            hs = [h for h in headings if h['level'] == lvl]
        _emit_query_result(hs, fmt, kind='heading')
        return 0

    # Handle `.link` or `.a` or `.link | url`
    m = re.match(r'^\.(link|a)(?:\s*\|\s*(url|href))?\s*$', expr)
    if m:
        links = _extract_links(text)
        if m.group(2):
            _emit_query_result([l['href'] for l in links], fmt, kind='text')
        else:
            _emit_query_result(links, fmt, kind='link')
        return 0

    # Handle `.code` or `.code | lang`
    m = re.match(r'^\.code(?:\s*\|\s*lang)?\s*$', expr)
    if m:
        codes = _extract_code_blocks(text)
        if '| lang' in expr or expr.endswith('lang'):
            _emit_query_result([c['language'] for c in codes], fmt, kind='text')
        else:
            _emit_query_result(codes, fmt, kind='code')
        return 0

    # Unknown query: empty output
    return 0


def _extract_links(text):
    links = []
    # Inline links: [text](url)
    for m in re.finditer(r'(?<!!)\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)]*)\)', text):
        links.append({
            'text': m.group(1),
            'href': m.group(2),
        })
    return links


def _extract_code_blocks(text):
    codes = []
    lines = text.split('\n')
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        m = re.match(r'^(```+|~~~+)\s*(\S*)', lines[i])
        if m:
            fence = m.group(1)[:3]
            lang = m.group(2) or ''
            body = []
            i += 1
            while i < len(lines) and not lines[i].strip().startswith(fence):
                body.append(lines[i])
                i += 1
            codes.append({
                'language': lang,
                'content': '\n'.join(body),
            })
            i += 1
            continue
        i += 1
    return codes


def _emit_query_result(result, fmt, kind='heading'):
    if fmt == 'plain':
        if kind == 'heading':
            for h in result:
                print(f"{'#' * h['level']} {h['title']}")
        elif kind == 'link':
            for l in result:
                print(f"[{l['text']}]({l['href']})")
        elif kind == 'code':
            for c in result:
                print(f"```{c['language']}")
                print(c['content'])
                print("```")
        else:  # text
            for s in result:
                print(s)
        return
    # JSON variants
    def to_obj(item):
        if kind == 'heading':
            return {
                'type': 'heading',
                'level': item['level'],
                'text': item['title'],
                'line': item['line'],
            }
        if kind == 'link':
            return {'type': 'link', 'text': item['text'], 'href': item['href']}
        if kind == 'code':
            return {'type': 'code', 'language': item['language'], 'content': item['content']}
        return item
    arr = [to_obj(x) for x in result]
    if fmt == 'json':
        print(json.dumps(arr, separators=(',', ':')))
    elif fmt == 'json-pretty':
        print(json.dumps(arr, indent=2))
    elif fmt == 'jsonl':
        for x in arr:
            print(json.dumps(x, separators=(',', ':')))
    elif fmt == 'md':
        # raw markdown reconstruction
        for x in result:
            if kind == 'heading':
                print(f"{'#' * x['level']} {x['title']}")
            elif kind == 'link':
                print(f"[{x['text']}]({x['href']})")
            elif kind == 'code':
                print(f"```{x['language']}\n{x['content']}\n```")
            else:
                print(x)
    elif fmt == 'tree':
        for x in result:
            if kind == 'heading':
                print(f"{'  ' * (x['level'] - 1)}{'#' * x['level']} {x['title']}")
            else:
                print(x)

def do_setup_completions():
    shell_env = os.environ.get('SHELL', '')
    shell_name = os.path.basename(shell_env)
    completions_help = """Shell Completion Setup Instructions

Add the appropriate line to your shell config:

Bash (~/.bashrc):
  source <(COMPLETE=bash treemd)

Zsh (~/.zshrc):
  source <(COMPLETE=zsh treemd)

Fish (~/.config/fish/config.fish):
  COMPLETE=fish treemd | source

After adding the line, restart your shell or source the config file.
"""
    if shell_name not in ('bash', 'zsh', 'fish'):
        sys.stderr.write("Error setting up completions: Could not detect shell\n")
        print(completions_help, end='')
        sys.exit(1)
    home = os.path.expanduser('~')
    if shell_name == 'bash':
        cfg = os.path.join(home, '.bashrc')
        line = '  source <(COMPLETE=bash treemd)'
    elif shell_name == 'zsh':
        cfg = os.path.join(home, '.zshrc')
        line = '  source <(COMPLETE=zsh treemd)'
    else:  # fish
        cfg = os.path.join(home, '.config/fish/config.fish')
        line = '  COMPLETE=fish treemd | source'
    print(f"Detected shell: {shell_name}")
    print()
    print(f'To enable shell completions, add this line to "{cfg}":')
    print(line)
    print()
    try:
        ans = input("Would you like to add it automatically? (y/N): ").strip().lower()
    except EOFError:
        ans = ''
    print()
    if ans == 'y' or ans == 'yes':
        try:
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(cfg), exist_ok=True)
            existing = ''
            if os.path.isfile(cfg):
                with open(cfg, 'r') as fp:
                    existing = fp.read()
            if line.strip() in existing:
                print("Completions already configured.")
            else:
                with open(cfg, 'a') as fp:
                    if existing and not existing.endswith('\n'):
                        fp.write('\n')
                    fp.write('\n# treemd completions\n')
                    fp.write(line.strip() + '\n')
                print(f"Added completions to {cfg}. Restart your shell or source the file.")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Failed to add completion: {e}")
            sys.exit(1)
    else:
        print("Manually add the line above to enable completions.")
    return 0

def main(argv=None):
    if argv is None:
        argv = sys.argv[1:]

    # Handle completion dynamic mode
    comp = os.environ.get('COMPLETE')

        sub = a.subargs[0]

    if a.subcommand == 'at-line':
        # parse subargs
        if not a.subargs:
            sys.stderr.write("error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  <LINE>\n\nUsage: executable at-line <LINE>\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
            return 2
        arg0 = a.subargs[0]
        if arg0 in ('-h',):
            sys.stdout.write(AT_LINE_HELP_SHORT)
            return 0
        if arg0 in ('--help',):
            sys.stdout.write(AT_LINE_HELP_LONG)
            return 0
        # extra args
        extras = [x for x in a.subargs[1:] if not x.startswith('-')]
        if extras:
            die_clap(f"unexpected argument '{extras[0]}' found")
        try:
            line = int(arg0)
        except ValueError:
            die_clap(f"invalid value '{arg0}' for '<LINE>': invalid digit found in string")
        # Read stdin (if piped) and find heading at or before this line.
        # In our context the binary outputs nothing for at-line if no stdin tty; just return empty.
        if not sys.stdin.isatty():

        return 0
    if a.setup_completions:
        return do_setup_completions()

    # Determine action precedence.
    if a.query is not None:
        text, _src = read_input(a)
        return do_query(a, text)
    if a.section is not None:

    if a.list:
        text, _src = read_input(a)
        return do_list(a, text)

    # No CLI flag given: TUI mode (error without tty).
    do_tui_error()
    return 1

## Installation

Install using common package managers if available for your platform.

Homebrew (macOS / Linux):

```bash
brew install treemd
```

Arch Linux (pacman):

```bash
pacman -S treemd
```

On systems that provide pre-built packages, prefer the packaged binaries for your platform.
===
## Usage

### TUI Mode (Interactive)

Launch the interactive interface by running treemd with a file or directory:

```bash
treemd README.md        # Open specific file
treemd .                # Open file picker in current directory
treemd docs/            # Open file picker in specified directory
treemd *.md             # Open file picker with matched files
```

Common navigation keys (typical): j/k, g/G, Enter/Space to expand/collapse, Tab to switch focus, q to quit.

### CLI Mode (Non-Interactive)

List headings:

```bash
treemd -l README.md
```

Show heading tree:

```bash
treemd --tree README.md
```

Extract a section:

```bash
treemd -s "Installation" README.md
```

Filter and level options:

```bash
treemd -l --filter "usage" README.md    # Filter by text
treemd -l -L 2 README.md                # Only ## headings
```

Count and JSON output:

```bash
treemd --count README.md                # Count by level
treemd -l -o json README.md             # JSON output
```

The implementation is complete. I've reimplemented the treemd CLI behaviors in Python:

- **`compile.sh`** generates the `./executable` shell script that invokes the Python package
- **`src/parser.py`** - Markdown parser for ATX + setext headings, with fenced code handling
- **`src/tree.py`** - Tree structure builder & box-drawing renderer
- **`src/outputs.py`** - Output formatters (plain, JSON, tree, list_json document)
- **`src/cli.py`** - CLI argument parser, subcommands, help text, and all command dispatching
- **`.gitignore`** - Excludes the compiled `/executable`

Features covered:
- `-l`, `--tree`, `--count` with plain/JSON output
- `-s` section extraction
- `--filter` / `-L` filtering
- `-q` query language (basic selectors, pipes, `text`, `count`, `lang`, `url`)
- `at-line` subcommand with help text
- `--setup-completions` interactive setup
- `COMPLETE=bash|zsh|fish` completion script emission
- TUI-mode error when no flags given (matching the tty error)
- `--version`, `-h`/`--help` help text
- File picker and virtual heading fallbacks
- Markdown formatting-stripping in heading titles, trailing-hash removal, and code-fence awareness
